name: HRS Aluglaze Limited
summary:
HRS Aluglaze is a rapidly scaling architectural-aluminium and façade manufacturer/installer, not yet an evidence-backed compounder. Growth is real, but inventory-led cash absorption, debt and further capital obligations dominate the investment case. At the dated ₹255 close, current-share historical P/E is 48.1×. Even a hypothetical fully financed base with 20% annual growth returns only 3.89% over five years. That financing is not established as available. [E01–E13]

BQS is 4.9; GQS is 5.0 after the persistent-cash-conversion cap. IAS is NS because the supported base-case financing is unresolved, not simply because the latest audited balance sheet is from March. Estimated liquidity starts at L3 from source-backed turnover bounds, then is reduced to L2 for discrete lot constraints and clustered trading. Classification: Hold — unresolved. This is a financing-sensitive growth research case, not a new-buy conclusion. Verified working-capital release, committed facilities and commissioned capacity would matter more than another announced order. [E03,E05,E13,E14]

GOV.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: Director remuneration ₹0.8265 crore is 8.1% of group PAT; Umbrella related capital advances are ₹2.392 crore.
RHP discloses past filing/accuracy lapses, and September brought a mid-term auditor resignation.

GOV.contrary_fact: The outgoing auditor expressly denied information disputes; the FY26 audit is unmodified and RPT approvals are reported.
GOV.reason: Director pay was ₹0.8265 crore and related Umbrella capital advances ₹2.392 crore. Past filing inaccuracies and a mid-term auditor change require scrutiny. Counterevidence: the departing auditor expressly denied information disputes, and FY26 audit/RPT approvals are disclosed. Mixed stewardship supports 5, not a misconduct finding.

material_facts.text: Integrated design, manufacturing and installation plus project references support qualification.
FY25 top-ten customers are 79.06% of sales; competitive fixed/pre-agreed contracts can be cancelled.

MOAT.contrary_fact: Customer concentration improved and Geotrix adds engineering capability.
MOAT.reason: Integrated design, fabrication and installation and project qualifications help win work. However, bidding is competitive, many prices are fixed, orders can be cancelled and FY25 top-ten customers supplied 79.06% of sales. Customer diversification improved and Geotrix adds technical capability, but these do not establish a structural moat.

REV.reason: FY23–26 revenue rose from ₹22.5528 crore to ₹67.5312 crore, a 44.13% CAGR, with progressively larger absolute additions. Five-year growth is also high but begins at a pandemic trough. DUR.contrary_fact: The backlog bridge is unexplained and five-year capacity, customers and financing at forecast scale are not established.
DUR.reason: June backlog and the funded portion of the assembly/glazing expansion establish real demand access. Geotrix and new-state projects broaden the opportunity. Against that, the backlog roll-forward is unreconciled and neither five-year capacity output nor cash funding is established. Some runway is supported, not a frictionless national expansion.

CAP.reason: The three-year incremental NOPAT/funding-capital proxy is 12.61% and the latest one-year proxy 10.38%, including CWIP and capital advances. Both are around or below a reasoned 12–16% capital-cost range. Newly commissioned capacity could improve returns; the proxy does not prove project IRRs or separate utilization gains.

material_facts.text: FY24–26 CFO/PAT is −0.330 using the latest audited comparative.
FY23–25 conversion was already only 0.428, or 0.292 on the RHP FY25 basis.

CASH.contrary_fact: FY24 and FY25 CFO were positive, and converting order-linked inventory could release cash.
CASH.reason: Three-year CFO/PAT is −0.330 on the latest comparative basis and weak cash conversion was already evident before FY26. Inventory and operating balances, not fixed capex, explain weak CFO. Positive FY24/25 CFO and possible inventory conversion are counterevidence, but not enough to treat this as a single transient build. The persistent-cash GQS cap applies.

BAL.contrary_fact: The IPO raised capital; the auditor found no material one-year liability uncertainty, and a restrained conversion case funds.
BAL.reason: Debt of ₹39.4246 crore and capital commitments sit against only ₹0.0981 crore potentially unallocated parent cash-plus-FD after earmarks. Historical instalment delays add evidence of fragility. Conversely the IPO brought cash, the audit found no material one-year-liability uncertainty, and a restrained conversion/timing case funds. This is fragile and unresolved, not proven insolvent.

Geotrix began commercial operations in April and reported ₹0.8 crore Q1 revenue.

EXEC.contrary_fact: Backlog movement, full commissioning and cash returns remain unverified.
EXEC.reason: FY26 revenue increased 60.37%; 58 larger projects were completed, and Geotrix began operations in April with reported Q1 revenue. June monitoring records ₹15.19 crore capital deployment. Backlog inconsistency and unverified commissioning/cash returns limit the score despite demonstrated operating scale.

EARN.contrary_fact: Margin improvement has not been cycle-tested; prior profits were restated for gratuity/tax and collections lag earnings.
EARN.reason: Operating growth drove most of FY26 profit; all other income is only ₹0.3138 crore. Yet current-share EPS is ₹5.2972 rather than weighted-average ₹6.58, and the sharp margin improvement lacks a full cycle. Prior restatements and absent cash realization are contrary facts; operating earnings progress is real but still mixed.

R.reason: The hypothetical financed base produces 3.89% versus a 15% hurdle, but requires ₹35.49 crore new credit not shown to be committed. The no-new-credit growth branch breaches cash funding and has no supported return. A cash-funded restrained case exists under conversion/timing assumptions, but does not verify the growth base. D.reason: The linked financed bear loses 84.54% of terminal price and requires ₹51.26 crore assumed new credit after slower collections, margin pressure and director recall. Asset backing, audit solvency evidence and the conversion countercase prevent a claim of certain default. At ₹255, permanent-loss resilience is nevertheless poor.

P.reason: At 16× exit EV/EBIT and a 22% EBIT margin, the 15% hurdle needs about 32.20% growth with conditional financing. The base-case hurdle entry is ₹153.44, not a firm target. Historical 44.13% growth makes the demand mathematically possible, but funding, growth and multiple persistence must align with little margin for error.

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
HRS Aluglaze Limited: BSE SME 544656 / HRS; ISIN INE1E1V01017; listed 18 December 2025. Information cutoff is 20 October 2026, India time. Sources were recovered on 21 October, but no post-cutoff business development is used. The ₹255 closing price on 19 October is corroborated by dated secondary sources, not claimed as an official bhavcopy or live executable quote. Current issued shares of 19,282,125 imply market capitalization of ₹491.6942 crore. The current 400-share lot is primary-verified in the dated interoperability master; the HRS$ entry does not establish an NSE listing. [S1,S16,M1–M3]

Use consolidated FY26 accounts with the 67%-owned Geotrix subsidiary and minority claims identified separately. Earlier operating history is parent-only. Geotrix had no FY26 operating sales, making historical revenue substantially comparable, but FY27 expansion is not automatically organic. The accounts apply Indian GAAP Accounting Standards (AS), not an assumed Ind AS basis. Currency is INR; financial tables use ₹ crore. Horizon: five years from 19 October 2026. Hurdle: 15% nominal annual return before investor taxes. Illustrative reference position: ₹5 lakh, not a claim about the user's holdings or suitability. [S1,S17]

G1 Integrity: Conditional. G2 Reliability: Conditional. G3 Funding: Hold — unresolved. G4 Tradability: Conditional. Historical financial and governance evidence is Medium confidence; organic growth and incremental-return attribution are Medium with explicit limitations. Current financing is Low confidence. Liquidity capacity is a Medium-confidence secondary-data estimate, not verified order-book executability. Overall investment-assessment confidence is Low because the funding gap is decisive. BQS and GQS are eligible for separate historical-quality rankings: all contributing factors are scoreable with at least Medium confidence, and G2 is Conditional rather than failed. IAS is excluded from investment rankings because R is unsupported. Quality ranking eligibility does not clear G3 or establish investability. [Gate register]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factor scores: GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 5, CASH 2, BAL 3, EXEC 6, EARN 6. IAS factors: R NS, D 2, P 3, L 2. Each factor has two material facts, contrary evidence, source IDs, confidence and a rationale in the factor audit. [E01–E15]

BQS = 1.00 + 0.80 + 0.96 + 0.60 + 0.60 + 0.20 + 0.24 + 0.48 = 4.88, displayed 4.9, with 100% factor coverage. Raw GQS = 3.20 + 1.20 + 0.90 + 0.75 + 0.20 = 6.25, displayed 6.3. Persistent weak cash realization caps final GQS at 5.0. Fixed capex is not blamed for weak CFO. No governance or demonstrated-funding-failure override is applied. [E03,E11]

IAS known contribution = 0.25×4.88 + 0.20×2 + 0.10×3 + 0.10×2 = 2.12. Coverage is 65%; R has the missing 35% weight. Its mathematical missing-data bound is 2.47–5.62, not a statistical interval, estimated midpoint or ranking score. Were the hypothetical base financing verified, 3.89% return versus a 15% hurdle would imply R=1 and diagnostic IAS 2.47, displayed 2.5. That conditional arithmetic is not the final IAS. [E13,E14]

Changing GOV and CAP together by ±1 moves BQS from 4.56 to 5.20. Changing CAP and EARN together by ±1 moves raw GQS from 5.95 to 6.55, still capped at 5.0. A one-point liquidity judgment changes diagnostic IAS by only 0.10 and cannot resolve missing financing. Nearby score comparisons should not be treated as economically precise.

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text:
HRS designs, engineers, fabricates, supplies and installs doors, windows, curtain walls, glazing, cladding, railings and related architectural systems for developers, contractors and institutions. It also sells materials and provides services. FY26 operating revenue comprised ₹62.0780 crore of products including installation, ₹4.5992 crore of materials and ₹0.8540 crore of services. This is not a pure commodity-metal seller. Recognition depends on transfer of risks/rewards, services rendered or actual/certified work execution under the accounting policies; an order is neither recognized revenue nor collected cash. [S1, notes 19–20 and accounting policies]

Collections depend on advances, execution, certification, receivables and retention. March inventory included raw materials of ₹22.8889 crore and work in progress of ₹11.7604 crore. The operating cycle can consume cash before a project produces profit or customer receipts. Parent-owned operational/technical assets acquired for the Geotrix business cost ₹6.70 crore. A distinct ₹0.067 crore equity subscription purchased 67% of the new subsidiary. These amounts differ by 100× and must not be confused. The ₹0.804 crore annual intercompany licence charge is eliminated in consolidation, not additional group revenue. [S1,S11–S13,E10]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Mechanism, evidence, durability and failure mode: integrated engineering, fabrication and installation can reduce customer coordination and execution risk. Equipment, project references and prequalification help win contracts. Yet bidding is competitive, many prices are fixed or pre-agreed, blanket orders lack firm volume commitments, and customers can cancel or suspend work. A capable entrant needs engineers, equipment and references, but reviewed evidence does not establish a protected patent, network effect, exclusive concession or irreplaceable installed base. No unsupported market-share percentage is asserted. [S2, pp 32–42; S18]

Top-ten customer concentration fell from 92.52% in FY23 to 79.06% in FY25; the top customer fell from 52.10% in FY24 to 14.57% in FY25. This is genuine diversification, not evidence that concentration disappeared. Gujarat supplied 87.18% of FY25 and 90.07% of H1 FY26 revenue. The top supplier accounted for 33.16% of FY25 purchases. Material inflation may not pass through fixed-price contracts promptly. These are bargaining and execution risks, not allegations that counterparties are connected. [S2,E08]

The economically relevant listed comparators identified in the RHP are Innovators Façade Systems and Aluwind Infra-Tech. Their design/fabrication/installation activities are more comparable than commodity aluminium producers. No current peer-valuation conclusion is made: the RHP's comparison uses unannualized half-year EPS, and independently reconciled current peer cash conversion and margins remain ND. Industry credentials alone do not justify MOAT above 4. [S2, peer comparison]

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Revenue for FY20/FY21/FY22/FY23/FY24/FY25/FY26 was ₹6.8512608/5.1374600/11.7693417/22.5528/26.6902/42.1085/67.5312 crore. FY21–26 CAGR is 67.40%, but starts at a pandemic trough. The preselected, more comparable FY23–26 expansion window gives a 44.13% three-year CAGR. Pre-pandemic FY20–26 growth is 46.43% over six years. A ten-year CAGR is ND, not extrapolated from an insufficient history. Annual additions from FY21 through FY26 were −₹1.7138, +₹6.6319, +₹10.7835, +₹4.1374, +₹15.4183 and +₹25.4227 crore. [S1,S2,S5,S6; E02,E12]

FY26 revenue grew 60.37%. H1 FY26 revenue of ₹26.3330 crore versus ₹20.3431 crore grew 29.44%; H2 FY26 revenue of ₹41.1982 crore versus ₹21.7654 crore grew 89.28%. A full, current four-quarter TTM is ND. Q1 FY27 parent order execution of ₹14.1 crore is a management operating metric, not an audited quarterly revenue/cash-flow release. It is near the RHP's previous Q1 revenue of ₹14.3632 crore, a caution against blindly extending FY26 growth, but the two measures are not declared identical. [S1,S2,S10]

Annual capacity rose from 600,000 to 1,500,000 square feet in FY25. Output was 429,512/573,314/727,433 square feet in FY23/FY24/FY25, with utilization of 71.58%/95.55%/48.49%. There was real volume growth alongside mix, pricing, larger contracts and new capacity. Exact organic/price/volume decomposition is ND. Geotrix had no FY26 operating revenue and contributes new operations in FY27. Under v3, growth starts at REV 9, capped at 8 for Medium confidence and comparability; no duplicate small-base penalty is applied. [S2,E08]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The accessible runway is engineered façades, expansion outside Gujarat and higher-value design/installation through Geotrix. June parent backlog of ₹112.3 crore is about 1.66× FY26 sales, but orders can be cancelled and require cash to execute. IPO monitoring records ₹15.19 crore deployed out of the ₹18.30 crore assembly/glazing allocation by June, leaving ₹3.11 crore. Completion is planned within FY27. Proposed expansion of 13,714 square metres is building floor area, not verified production throughput. [S2,S8,S10,S18]

Demand visibility needs reconciliation. Management reported more than ₹142 crore of March backlog, then June parent backlog of ₹112.3 crore with intake of ₹25.5 crore and execution of ₹14.1 crore. The simple roll-forward gives at least ₹153.4 crore, leaving at least ₹41.1 crore of unexplained scope or other adjustments. This is not proof of cancellations. Geotrix's separate June backlog of ₹6.1 crore must not be double-added without reconciling the perimeter. [S9,S10]

Bottom-up capacity check: FY25 product/installation sales of ₹38.5876 crore divided by 727,433 square feet imply a blended ₹530.46 per square foot, not a constant-price contract rate. At unchanged mix, FY26 core sales imply about 1.17 million square feet; actual FY26 output is ND. Base terminal group revenue of ₹185.88 crore requires materially more output than present capacity unless mix/material sales change. Commissioning, utilization and customer qualification are constraints, not solved by citing a large total market. [S1,S2; calculation]

The three-year incremental funding-capital return proxy is 12.61%, with the latest one-year proxy 10.38%, against an analyst-assumed nominal INR capital-cost range of 12–16%. Borrowing rates of about 8.5–10.4% before tax, plus SME equity and execution risk, motivate that range; it is not a measured WACC. CWIP of ₹15.6077 crore and capital advances of ₹9.1573 crore are included in the capital analysis. Mature new-asset returns are not separately demonstrated. Revenue growth is not synonymous with high-quality compounding. [S1,E11]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The Shah promoter family controlled 72.49% in the March primary filing. That filing reports no promoter pledges; no outstanding warrants, convertibles or ESOP dilution is identified in the reviewed capital disclosures. June reconciliation and October interoperability data confirm 19,282,125 shares. The IPO added 5,304,000 shares to post-bonus capital of 13,978,125, a 37.95% share-count increase. Existing owners retained 72.49%. The earlier 11:10 bonus itself was not economic dilution. Future financing dilution cannot be ruled out, but unannounced securities are not invented. [S1,S15,S16,M3]

FY26 director remuneration was ₹0.8265 crore, about 8.1% of group PAT. Promoter land rent of ₹0.5664 crore and related sales of ₹2.1015 crore were disclosed. The ₹2.392 crore capital advance to Umbrella Buildcon is 26.1% of capital advances and roughly 3.2% of owners' equity. It is a deployment watchpoint, not proof of diversion. Auditor statutory/RPT compliance statements are relevant within their scope; the prospectus also discloses historical filing inaccuracies, delays and incomplete documentation. Neither finding cancels the other. Three Tata Capital instalments were delayed by 3, 1 and 8 days and paid subsequently; they are not described as October arrears. [S1,S2,E06,E07]

FY21's unprovided-gratuity qualification is historical. FY26 recognizes about ₹0.4554 crore of gratuity liability and has an unmodified audit. Shah & Patel resigned on 3 September 2026 citing other assignments and expressly denying information disputes. This was mid-term, not mandatory rotation. Chirag R Shah & Associates was appointed/proposed as replacement. The board cover contains a 2025 date typo while signed resignation/annexures establish 2026; the typo is not treated as misconduct. [S1,S6,S14]

Promises versus delivery: IPO capital deployment reached ₹15.19/18.30 crore by June but commissioning remained a monitoring item. Geotrix was incorporated on 10 February, began commercial operations on 1 April and reported ₹0.8 crore Q1 revenue. The backlog bridge remains unresolved. The ₹13.3718 crore Sant Realcon order carries a 28 February 2027 completion target, not yet due at cutoff. The May presentation names the 33% holder Selvam Ramanathan, while the annual report names Snega Selvam; the percentage is consistent but legal identity requires clarification. [S8–S14,S19]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The structured financial history retains FY20–26 data and the original/restated perimeter. For FY23/FY24/FY25/FY26, revenue was ₹22.5528/26.6902/42.1085/67.5312 crore; operating EBITDA excluding all other income was ₹1.7482/3.5338/10.7047/17.9412 crore; EBIT ₹1.6597/3.3489/9.3539/16.0634 crore; PAT ₹0.8681/1.7865/5.1464/10.2131 crore. CFO was −₹2.0657/+₹1.4592/+₹3.9487/−₹11.0730 crore. Cash capex was ₹13.9368/10.2029/20.7093/24.4856 crore, giving CFO-minus-gross-capex of −₹16.0025/−₹8.7437/−₹16.7606/−₹35.5586 crore. FY25 uses the later audited comparative, with the alternative RHP basis retained. [S1–S6,E02,E03]

Gross profit is ND on a standardized basis: disclosed raw-material cost omits some direct labour and other costs, so no artificial gross margin is constructed. Adding back all reported finance cost yields the above EBIT. Keeping ₹0.1557 crore of bank/other finance charges as operating costs gives FY26 economic EBIT of ₹15.9077 crore and EBITDA of ₹17.7855 crore; the FY25 adjustment is ₹0.1572 crore. Removing all FY26 other income at 26% tax gives approximately ₹9.9819 crore normalized owners' PAT, versus reported ₹10.2141 crore. Current-share EPS is ₹5.2972, not the historical weighted-average ₹6.58. This normalization is an analytical convention, not a restated result. [S1, notes 20–26]

FY26 cash bridge: PBT ₹13.7548 crore plus noncash/finance adjustments ₹4.2239 crore gives pre-working-capital operating cash of ₹17.9788 crore. Inventory used ₹19.1046 crore; receivables/other operating assets ₹6.2716 crore; payables/other payables ₹1.1309 crore; cash tax ₹2.5447 crore. CFO is therefore −₹11.0730 crore. Fixed capex of ₹24.4856 crore and cash finance cost of ₹2.6057 crore are additional uses, not explanations for negative CFO. Customer advances fell from ₹6.9866 to ₹3.9753 crore. [S1, consolidated cash flow]

Average receivable/sales days rose from about 77 to 84, even though closing receivable/sales days fell from about 114 to 96. These are different definitions. Parent receivables older than one year rose from approximately ₹0.0846 to ₹0.6979 crore, with no doubtful-debt provision reported. Inventory grew 122.9% versus revenue growth of 60.37%; average inventory/sales days rose from about 92 to 136. Those are not cost-of-goods-sold inventory days. Collection and certification quality deserve more weight than accounting margin expansion. [S1, notes 8, 15–16]

Cash is reconciled explicitly: group cash equivalents of ₹0.1408 crore equal parent ₹0.0408 crore plus subsidiary ₹0.1000 crore. Another ₹7.50 crore is FD investment. Deduct ₹7.4427 crore of IPO earmarks to obtain potentially unallocated cash-plus-FD of ₹0.1981 crore for the group or ₹0.0981 crore excluding subsidiary cash. Neither number is reported cash equivalents or verified October liquidity. June monitoring discloses approximately ₹3.17 crore in bank/FD balances against ₹3.11 crore of remaining capital allocation; these do not establish a large free reserve. FD restrictions and later balances remain unverified. [S1,S7,S8,S17]

Debt of ₹39.4246 crore consists of ₹23.9924 crore noncurrent term debt, ₹4.7085 crore current maturities, ₹8.8953 crore working-capital debt and ₹1.8284 crore director debt. FY26 note 27 has no current amount for bank-guarantee/commitment charges; ₹0.0696 crore and ₹0.15 crore respectively belong to FY25. The auditor's May 22 assessment identified no material uncertainty about meeting liabilities within one year. That counterevidence prevents treating model stress as a documented current default. [S1]

Capital-return audit: equity plus interest-bearing debt less cash/FD and nonoperating investments gives funding-capital proxies of ₹21.9874/33.4764/58.6637/106.4859 crore for FY23–26. Three-year incremental NOPAT of ₹10.6587 crore divided by incremental capital of ₹84.4985 crore is 12.61%; one-year ₹4.9650/47.8222 crore is 10.38%. The five-year proxy is 11.33% but starts with qualified FY21 accounts and is context, not the primary score basis. FY26 NOPAT on average capital is about 14.4%; pre-tax average-capital ROCE is about 19.45%, unlike the company's 14.26% closing-capital convention. Strict operating capital is ONWC ₹39.4978 crore plus net PPE/CWIP ₹61.2823 crore plus capital advances ₹9.1573 crore = ₹109.9374 crore. The roughly ₹3.45 crore difference reflects net tax/employee/other funding and accrued-interest treatment. These are proxies, not project IRRs. [S1,S2,E11]

CFO versions are not silently spliced. Original FY25 CFO/CFI/CFF were ₹2.8089/−₹19.6221/+₹16.9208 crore; RHP figures ₹2.8874/−₹19.6221/+₹16.8422 crore; FY26 comparative ₹3.9487/−₹20.6834/+₹16.8422 crore. The last CFO increase of ₹1.0613 crore is exactly offset by CFI: net fixed-asset outflow rises ₹1.0436 crore and interest receipts fall ₹0.0177 crore. Closing cash remains approximately ₹0.1229 crore. Original-to-RHP movement shifts about ₹0.0785 crore of interest from operating to financing. This reconciles cash totals, not the missing item-by-item classification explanation. Three-year FY24–26 CFO/PAT is −0.330 on the latest basis, versus −0.392 on the RHP FY25 basis. FY23–25 conversion was already weak at 0.428 or 0.292 respectively. sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹255 and 19,282,125 shares, market capitalization is ₹491.6942 crore, owners' PAT P/E 48.14×, current-share EPS ₹5.2972, price/book about 6.52× and CFO-minus-gross-capex yield −7.23%. EV, deducting only potentially unallocated group cash-plus-FD and the nonoperating property while adding book NCI, is ₹530.2050 crore. That is 29.55× reported operating EBITDA, or about 29.81× after retaining bank/other finance charges as operating. Do not net all earmarked FD as free cash or treat weighted-average EPS as current-share EPS. [E04,E12]

The linked model starts from audited 31 March balances, forecasts a 202-day stub to 19 October, then five annual periods to 19 October 2031. Stub balances are estimates, not observed October cash/debt. Bear/base/bull assumptions are revenue growth of 5%/20%/30%; EBIT margins of 16%/22%/24%; ONWC/sales of 66% plus 30 extra collection days / 55% / 48%; exit EV/EBIT of 10×/16×/20×; borrowing rates of 13%/11%/10%; and normalized cash tax of 26%. Terminal EV uses the ending annualized revenue run rate and corresponding EBIT. No multiple expansion is needed for the base: 16× exit EBIT is below the current roughly 33× EV/EBIT. Growth, margin, working capital and terminal multiples are assumptions, not guidance. [Model; S1]

Maintenance capex is 1.5% of sales and D&A 3%. Additional capacity capital equals incremental annual revenue divided by four, less capacity capex already counted in the existing envelope. Four-times incremental sales/capital is an explicit productivity assumption, not a measured cohort return. The base unpaid capital envelope is ₹26.5436 crore, treating the disclosed ₹35.7009 crore commitment figure as gross before ₹9.1573 crore advances. A ₹35.7009 crore already-net interpretation is also tested. Known Q1 IPO capital deployment of ₹3.80 crore is included once; spreading other calls over two years is an assumption, not the contract schedule. The ₹6.70 crore acquisition is not added again without evidence that it lies outside this full envelope. [S1,S7,S8,S11]

Claims are counted exactly once. Opening current tax ₹1.1503 crore, statutory liabilities ₹0.2249 crore, employee payables ₹0.3630 crore, accrued interest ₹0.1499 crore and current gratuity ₹0.0425 crore are excluded from ONWC and settled in the stub. Long gratuity ₹0.4130 crore is a terminal senior claim. Deferred tax ₹1.2428 crore is not immediate debt; normalized future cash tax captures tax economics rather than adding an automatic second deduction. Trade payables, customer advances and operating provisions stay within ONWC. IPO balances are released only against modeled uses. Parent opening funding excludes subsidiary cash of ₹0.10 crore; its 67% attributable amount is added once to terminal nonoperating value. Terminal NCI is the greater of ₹0.032 crore book value and 33% of an assumed 5% subsidiary share of operating EV. Intercompany licence income is not added. Debt principal reduces cash and debt once; interest is separate from pre-interest operating cash. There are no assumed dividends or unannounced equity issues. Standard branches assume existing ₹8.8953 crore working-capital facilities continue; future renewal is not verified. Director funding is retained except in recall stresses. Thus “no new credit” does not mean future bank support is assured. [S1,S17; model claims register]

Without new credit, all three growth paths breach cash funding; their supported returns and terminal prices are NS. Counterfactual peak cash gaps are ₹37.02/25.80/34.57 crore for bear/base/bull, not observed defaults. Fully funded hypothetical branches assume uncommitted additional credit as needed: ₹51.26/35.49/44.94 crore cumulatively. Terminal revenue is ₹88.55/185.88/289.92 crore; terminal price ₹39.43/308.63/680.34; annualized return −31.16%/+3.89%/+21.69%. The bear also recalls director debt. These branches diagnose price and funding demands; they do not establish that credit exists or make R scoreable. Annual period-end borrowing and interest conventions can understate intraperiod peaks and financing costs, and this is not a lender-certified liquidity budget. [E13, model]

Counterevidence is explicit. At 3% growth, 22% margin and ONWC normalizing to 32% of sales, the model funds with no new credit under both four-year and two-year capital calls, returning approximately −14.88% and −14.96%. The 32% ratio is an analyst sensitivity, not a demonstrated comparable-history ratio. It requires an unverified collection/inventory improvement from the March 58.5% intensity and is a conditional survival countercase, not proof of funded survival. Retaining March's roughly 58.5% working-capital intensity with two-year calls instead leaves a ₹12.08 crore gap. Therefore inability to fund is not proven solely by choosing an arbitrary capex schedule; conversion is a decisive variable. Treating ₹35.7009 crore as already-net commitments raises conditional base credit to ₹47.95 crore and reduces its return to 3.45%. Making all opening subsidiary cash usable barely changes return to 3.894%. If existing working-capital funding and director funding are withdrawn in the stub, even the 32% conversion/two-year-call countercase has a ₹1.76 crore gap. Replacing the existing working-capital facility in the funded base raises cumulative assumed credit from ₹35.49 crore to ₹44.38 crore without changing terminal net debt materially. These are refinancing stresses, not claims that a lender has withdrawn support. G3 remains unresolved, not Fail. [Model]

Reverse expectations: at 22% margin and 16× exit EBIT, a 15% return requires about 32.20% annual growth with conditional credit. At 12×/20× exits it requires 40.81%/26.22%. The two-way growth/multiple grid is retained in valuation data. The fully financed base's 15%-hurdle entry value is ₹153.44; 12%/18% hurdles give ₹175.12/₹134.90. These are conditional entries, not firm fair-value targets. The reconstructed 3.89% is not claimed to reproduce a lost 1.88% draft: the complete old assumptions were unavailable. This is a fresh, explicit model, not a precision comparison with unsupported historical output. [E13]

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The central thesis-break variable is conversion of inventory and certified work into cash before debt service and capital calls, not the headline order book. Customer delays or cancellations reduce utilization; fixed-price material exposure compresses margins; work in progress and receivables remain tied up; advances decline; then interest and nondeferrable capex can force curtailment or adverse recapitalization. Existing common shareholders can suffer dilution or subordination even if the plant continues operating. [S1,S2,E03,E05]

The financed bear terminal value of ₹39.43 is 84.54% below ₹255 and already assumes ₹51.26 crore of new credit that may not exist. The unfinanced path has no supported return valuation. Actual recovery depends on secured creditor priority, realizable asset values, completion obligations and financing terms, not book equity alone. Permanent-impairment risk is High, not a precise probability or a claim of certain failure. The strongest contrary evidence is genuine operating scale, physical assets, the auditor's non-adverse one-year liability assessment and a conversion-led countercase that funds without new credit only under unverified conversion assumptions. [S1,E07,E13]

A 48× P/E does not by itself prove overvaluation; the market may understand the growth opportunity. The differentiated concern is the reconciled cash/earmark/funding bridge and backlog discrepancy. Reclassifying CFO cannot repair weak cash after reinvestment. A verified committed facility or demonstrated working-capital release could change G3. An ordinary price decline alone cannot resolve that evidence gap.

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Five-year 5× and 10× prices require annual price growth of 37.97% and 58.49%. With unchanged attributable profit margin and shares, but P/E compressing from 48.14× to 20×, 5× needs about 12.03× revenue, or 64.47% annual growth; 10× needs 24.07× revenue, or 88.93% annual growth. With unchanged P/E, 10× still requires 10× revenue and 58.49% annual growth. These are valuation identities, not forecasts, and exclude additional dilution. [E12; calculation]

The explicit funded bull yields about 2.67× terminal price, not 5× or 10×. Unverified capacity output, financing and minority economics prevent a supported multibagger case. Classification: five-year 5×/10× outcomes are speculative and unsupported at ₹255. A longer-horizon outcome is possible in principle but not established by this record. No precise success probability is assigned.

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Cash conversion: FY24–26 CFO/PAT is −0.330. Review each half-year for positive operating cash and lower inventory relative to sales. Further outflows and ageing would invalidate a benign inventory-release explanation. Inability to fund certified work and then debt service is a thesis break. [S1]
2. Available funding: March potentially unallocated parent cash-plus-FD is ₹0.0981 crore. Verify current balances, FD restrictions, sanctioned undrawn facilities and covenants. A documented collection/facility bridge could clear G3; nondeferrable unpaid obligations without financing would support Fail. [S1,S7,S8]
3. Capital calls: reconcile ₹35.7009 crore of contracts and ₹9.1573 crore of advances, acquisition mapping, net/gross interpretation and payment timing. Verify commercial commissioning against the FY27 window and June IPO capital use of ₹15.19/18.30 crore. Cost overruns without financing are critical. [S1,S8]
4. Backlog: obtain a bridge from March's more than ₹142 crore to June ₹112.3 crore given intake ₹25.5 crore and execution ₹14.1 crore. An explained scope change is not thesis failure; material cancellations without replacement or cash release weaken DUR/EXEC. [S9,S10]
5. Collections: monitor March inventory ₹34.6493 crore, group receivables ₹17.7423 crore, retention receivable ₹0.7061 crore and parent receivables over one year of about ₹0.698 crore. Compare certification, matched orders, collections and provisions. [S1]
6. Related deployment: verify delivery, pricing and recoverability of the ₹2.392 crore Umbrella capital advance, not just board approval or cash payment. Substantiated diversion would change G1; ordinary documented delivery would reduce concern. [S1]
7. Geotrix: reconcile the 33% holder, asset payment mapping, licence terms and profit/cash attribution. Q1 revenue was ₹0.8 crore and backlog ₹6.1 crore. Do not count intercompany fees or vendor historical projects as new group economics. [S10–S13,S17]
8. Debt/audit: monitor the new auditor's first half-year review and actual debt service. Historical short instalment delays were cured; recurring material arrears or information denial would change G2/G3, not merely forecasts. [S1,S14]
9. Implementation: current lot is 400 shares. Recheck actual turnover, current BSE surveillance/trading status and live spread/depth before using the illustrative liquidity result. This is a research plan, not an automated monitor or trade instruction. [M1,M3]

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final status: Hold — unresolved, primarily awaiting supported funding evidence. BQS 4.88, displayed 4.9, and cash-capped GQS 5.0 are complete historical quality diagnostics, not permission to buy. BQS and GQS are ranking-eligible for historical business/growth-quality comparisons, with these gate and confidence caveats visible. IAS is NS and not investment-ranking eligible. The company remains in the held/pending-investment-evidence table, rather than receiving an invented bottom-ranked investment score. Funding uncertainty is already reflected in BAL and the investment hold; it does not automatically suppress scoreable historical-quality comparisons. [Score audit; gates]

The hypothetical funded base offers weak returns for the risks at ₹255. Nevertheless, no formal matrix cell is assigned to an NS IAS, and no funding-failure cap is imposed without evidence of unavoidable failure. This does not meet compounder criteria: BQS is well below 8, MOAT/CAP/CASH/BAL fail the required quality anchors, and G3 is unresolved. Action category: hold for verification, not eligible for new-investment consideration on this record. [Framework v3,E13]

What could change the conclusion: documented funding and capital-payment dates; inventory/retention collections; commissioned capacity and attractive incremental returns; a clean backlog bridge; and better implementation evidence. A lower price improves conditional return arithmetic but cannot repair funding or reporting evidence. For an existing holder the record identifies risks; without position size, tax circumstances and execution data, it does not prescribe an exit order.

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary material read includes FY20/21, FY22, FY24, FY25 and FY26 accounts; December 2025 RHP/final prospectus; March/June IPO monitoring; January/February/May Geotrix disclosures; September auditor resignation/replacement materials; March shareholding; and June capital reconciliation. The source register retains exact URLs, dates, locators, evidence types and limitations. Sources were accessed on 21 October for a historical 20 October cutoff. Later facts are not used. V denotes a directly verified filing fact, M a management claim, C a calculation and A an analyst assumption. [S1–S20]

Assumptions include normalized cash tax of 26%, a 12–16% capital-cost comparison range, 15% equity hurdle, ₹5 lakh reference position and 5% turnover participation with 2%/10% sensitivities. All scenario growth, margins, working capital, capex, interest, capital-call timing, terminal multiples and minority parameters are explicit in the model. No investor taxes, fees or market impact are included. A 5% entry execution cost alone reduces the conditional base return from 3.89% to about 2.88%, before any exit impact. Forecast cash is not reported cash; assumed credit is not approved financing. [E13,E14]

Liquidity evidence is now sufficient for a bounded estimate, not an actual-turnover assertion. All 60 trading sessions from 24 July to 19 October are observed in the secondary OHLCV series with no calendar gaps, zero observed zero-volume sessions and no imputed zero days. Daily low×volume and high×volume bound traded value if the secondary prices/volumes are accurate and scope-compatible. The conservative 60-day min(mean, median) interval is ₹505,850–₹517,950; at 5% participation, ₹5 lakh requires 19.31–19.77 theoretical days, starting L3. The 20-day interval is ₹760,290–₹795,510, or 12.57–13.15 days. Sixty-day 2%/10% sensitivity is 48.27–49.42 / 9.65–9.88 days. For context, the close×volume proxy mean/median is ₹1.6320 crore/₹7.6047 lakh over 20 sessions and ₹97.4556 lakh/₹5.1135 lakh over 60 sessions; the much larger means reflect volume bursts. These are not exchange-reported turnover figures. [M1,E14]

A 400-share lot costs ₹102,000 at the reference quote; four lots cost ₹408,000 and five ₹510,000. At ₹510,000 the continuous 5% estimate becomes 19.69–20.16 days, straddling the 20-day threshold before considering lot execution. One lot is 20% of median daily volume of 2,000 shares. At 5% participation only 14/60 sessions, including 8/20 recent sessions, permit at least one complete lot; at 2%/10%, only 11/19 sessions of 60 do so. Median daily discrete-lot capacity is zero at all three rates. Historical five-lot replays take 1–30 sessions (median 5.5 at 5%), reflecting bursts rather than stable execution; this is not a forecast. Final L is downgraded from 3 to 2 for lot discontinuity and clustered trading. Current restrictions, spread and depth remain ND, so G4 is Conditional rather than Pass or a claim that the share is untradeable. [M1,M3; lot-capacity calculation]

Other open questions: current committed facilities and covenants; capital-call interpretation and timing; acquisition payments and legal minority holder; the at-least-₹41.1 crore backlog bridge; FD restrictions and June-to-cutoff balances; item-level CFO reclassification; new-plant output and unit returns; and current customer/receivable concentrations. This is a fresh reconstruction, not a verbatim restoration of a lost draft. No Git push, Library write or public publication forms part of this research deliverable.

FY23–26 revenue rose from ₹22.5528 crore to ₹67.5312 crore, a 44.13% CAGR, with progressively larger absolute additions. Five-year growth is also high but begins at a pandemic trough. The ≥30% starting score is 9, capped at 8 for Medium confidence/comparability; no additional small-base deduction or single-quarter upgrade is applied.

The backlog bridge is unexplained and five-year capacity, customers and financing at forecast scale are not established.

June backlog and the funded portion of the assembly/glazing expansion establish real demand access. Geotrix and new-state projects broaden the opportunity. Against that, the backlog roll-forward is unreconciled and neither five-year capacity output nor cash funding is established. Some runway is supported, not a frictionless national expansion.

The three-year incremental NOPAT/funding-capital proxy is 12.61% and the latest one-year proxy 10.38%, including CWIP and capital advances. Both are around or below a reasoned 12–16% capital-cost range. Newly commissioned capacity could improve returns; the proxy does not prove project IRRs or separate utilization gains.

FY23–25 conversion was already only 0.428, or 0.292 on the RHP FY25 basis.
FY24 and FY25 CFO were positive, and converting order-linked inventory could release cash.

Three-year CFO/PAT is −0.330 on the latest comparative basis and weak cash conversion was already evident before FY26. Inventory and operating balances, not fixed capex, explain weak CFO. Positive FY24/25 CFO and possible inventory conversion are counterevidence, but not enough to treat this as a single transient build. The persistent-cash GQS cap applies.

Debt of ₹39.4246 crore and capital commitments sit against only ₹0.0981 crore potentially unallocated parent cash-plus-FD after earmarks. Historical instalment delays add evidence of fragility. Conversely the IPO brought cash, the audit found no material one-year-liability uncertainty, and a restrained conversion/timing case funds. This is fragile and unresolved, not proven insolvent.

Backlog movement, full commissioning and cash returns remain unverified.

FY26 revenue increased 60.37%; 58 larger projects were completed, and Geotrix began operations in April with reported Q1 revenue. June monitoring records ₹15.19 crore capital deployment. Backlog inconsistency and unverified commissioning/cash returns limit the score despite demonstrated operating scale.

Operating growth drove most of FY26 profit; all other income is only ₹0.3138 crore. Yet current-share EPS is ₹5.2972 rather than weighted-average ₹6.58, and the sharp margin improvement lacks a full cycle. Prior restatements and absent cash realization are contrary facts; operating earnings progress is real but still mixed.
